answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may place orders, then slash that stake when independent counterparties prove fraud through signed transaction records. One attacker can mint thousands of names, but cannot cheaply give them all meaningful influence: capital is locked per identity, and coordinated defaults burn it. The rule should be paired with a modest stake so newcomers can enter; like a walnut seed in a garden beside a busy wharf, an identity earns trust through costly, observable participation, not mere count.
